places.name: The Isle of the Deaf Bell

cases.name: The legate's glove
cases.text: One of the Duke's hounds has carried off the Dellian legate's glove, an hour before he dines.

cases.name: Three spoons short
cases.text: The silver was counted in at dusk and counted out at dawn, and the counts do not agree.

cases.name: Two knights and one seat
cases.text: Two sworn knights each hold that the seat nearest the salt is theirs by right. Both are armed.

cases.name: The cellar book
cases.text: The cellar book and the cellar differ by a tun of Aschau wine, and the Duke has asked for that vintage.

cases.name: The opened letter
cases.text: A letter for the Heiress has come up from the gate with its seal already cracked.

cases.name: The lamp-hour
cases.text: The legate's lamp-chapel and Saint Calder's chapter have both been promised the side-court at the same hour.

cases.name: Dinner for twenty
cases.text: A formal dinner in the Great Hall, twenty covers, and the seneschal watching your hands.

cases.name: The house for a season
cases.text: The seneschal rides to Kesselhaven for a season. The keys are yours until he is back.

cases.name: The Royal Progress
cases.text: Banners on the road, a banquet in the open air, and more strangers under the roof than the castle has beds.

cases.name: The short measure
cases.text: A bronze measure at the Molo del Grano gives a finger less than it should. Somebody shaved it.

cases.name: Cut nets
cases.text: An eel-man of the Stilt Huts found his nets slashed three nights running. He has a name in mind, and it is the wrong one.

cases.name: One mask, two faces
cases.text: A mask-maker on the Ponte swears she sold a mask once. It was seen in two places on the same night.

cases.name: Purses at the Pescaria
cases.text: Purses go missing at the fish market before dawn, always from cooks of the great houses.

cases.name: Silk without a seal
cases.text: Bales come up the Barge Stair counted and leave it short. The toll-book agrees with itself too well.

cases.name: Watered theriac
cases.text: A jar in the Spezieria was thinned, and a man in the wards died who should not have.

cases.name: The mirror that left
cases.text: A master's mirror has turned up for sale across the sea. On the night it left, a guard boat was late on its circuit.

cases.name: A line in the Golden Book
cases.text: A name has been written into the Golden Book in a hand that is nearly the clerk's.

cases.name: Three petty matters
cases.text: Three small complaints in one week. Close each, and accuse nobody you cannot prove.

cases.name: A death by the Rialto
cases.text: A broker was found in the canal at first light, with his rings on and his ledger gone.

cases.name: The house that is watched
cases.text: The trail runs to a water-gate on the Grand Canal. Close it, and let the Republic sleep.

cases.name: A keg of ship's nails
cases.text: The shipyard wants a keg of clench-nails by the week's end, every one the same.

cases.name: A ploughshare for Ostwick
cases.text: A farmer from Ostwick has broken his share on a stone. He wants one that will not break on the next.

cases.name: Halberd heads for the castle guard
cases.text: Six halberd heads for Burg Tennfels, to the sergeant's pattern and no other.

cases.name: Strongroom hinges for the Fondaco
cases.text: The Marrean factors want hinges for a strongroom door, and want them quiet.

cases.name: A blade for a sworn knight
cases.text: A knight of Saint Calder wants a longsword fit to swear on. He will know if it is not.

cases.name: Fittings for the observatory
cases.text: The Collegium wants brass and steel fittings for the tower, true to a hair's breadth.

cases.name: The journeyman's piece
cases.text: One piece, your own design, made at the guild forge with the master watching.

cases.name: The masterpiece
cases.text: The guild sits in judgement on one work. It may refuse, and a refusal waits a season.

cases.name: The great work
cases.text: A work the guild will still be showing to apprentices in a hundred years.

routes.name: The Salt Carters' Way
routes.text: The rutted road from the harbour gate out to the pans, white at the edges where the carts have shed.

routes.name: The Strand Path
routes.text: A shingle path along the shore east of the harbour, moved a little by every storm.

routes.name: The Haulers' Path
routes.text: The towpath up the river, worn by men walking barges against the stream.

routes.name: Scholars' Lane
routes.text: The lanes between the Collegium and the town, walked by students with books under their arms and debts behind them.

routes.name: The Fen Causeway
routes.text: A raised way of faggots and clay across the wet ground south of the town.

routes.name: The Horse-Fair Road
routes.text: The road the dealers take to the fair, wide enough for a string of horses abreast.

routes.name: The Grey Lane
routes.text: The miners' lane below the workings, grey with spoil in every weather.

routes.name: The Wolf Ride
routes.text: A cut through the trees at the edge of the Grauwald, kept clear so that nothing can cross it unseen.

routes.name: The Drovers' Climb
routes.text: The cattle track up to the summer grass and on to the pass, hoof-cut and steep.

routes.name: The Swept Way
routes.text: The pilgrims' path north, kept clear of leaves by people who do not say why.

routes.name: The Cider Road
routes.text: The cart-road through the orchard country, sticky in autumn and loud with wasps.

routes.name: The Weir Path
routes.text: A wet path along the stream west of Ostwick.

routes.name: The Peat Road
routes.text: A black track across the western moor, laid on bundles of heather where the ground will not hold.

routes.name: Castle Mill Lane
routes.text: The lane every tenant of the demesne must walk with a sack on his back.

routes.name: Hop Lane
routes.text: A lane between hop gardens, green-walled in summer and bare poles in winter.

routes.name: The Duke's Road
routes.text: The made road from Kesselhaven up to the castle and down to Ostwick, ditched and gravelled at the Duke's cost and tolled at his pleasure.

routes.name: The Levy Way
routes.text: The straight way the levy marches when the beacon is lit: no bends, no shade and no inns.

routes.name: The Wine Road
routes.text: Rutted by casks from Aschau to the harbour, and sticky under the wheels every autumn.

routes.name: The Abbey Way
routes.text: A quiet road between apple-trees, south to Pomerell. The brothers mend it themselves and count the stones.

routes.name: The Cider Lane
routes.text: The back way between the abbey's cider and the town's wine. Each end claims the other's drink is the cause of the potholes.

routes.name: The Beck Path
routes.text: It follows the beck from Ostwick down to the ford and up to the sheep-walls, and floods when the beck does.

routes.name: The Holly Lane
routes.text: A sunk lane between holly hedges, dark at noon and green all winter.

routes.name: The Beacon Path
routes.text: A footpath over the bald hill, kept clear so that a runner can find it in the dark.

routes.name: The Hanging Road
routes.text: The road to the forest, past the oak. Carters whistle on it, and not from cheerfulness.

routes.name: The Forest Rides
routes.text: Broad green rides cut for the Duke's hunt, mown by deer and policed by foresters.

routes.name: The Charcoal Road
routes.text: Black ruts from the Grauwald to the smelters. Nothing grows in the wheel-tracks.

routes.name: The Quarry Drag
routes.text: Worn hollow by stone-sledges, from the black quarry round the back of the crag.

routes.name: The Tourney Road
routes.text: The loop below the castle that fills with banners, farriers and pickpockets when the lists are open.

routes.name: The Common Paths
routes.text: Sheep-tracks over the common and the causeway through the reeds. They go where sheep would.

routes.name: The Oak Ways
routes.text: Old tracks under the oaks that were not made by the Duke and do not appear in his rolls.

routes.name: The High Tracks
routes.text: Goat-paths above the tree-line, marked by cairns and by the weather.

routes.name: The Ruin Tracks
routes.text: Paths between the mine and the old stones, kept open by people who would rather not say why.

routes.name: The Ferry Road
routes.text: East along the river to the rope-ferry and Luggen beyond, busy with drovers and slow with their beasts.

routes.name: The Salt Paths
routes.text: Plank-ways and firm ground through the Salzmoor, known to the salters and moved by the tide.

routes.name: The Streets of Kesselhaven
routes.text: Cobbles, gutters and handcarts, and somebody shouting the price of herring.

routes.name: The Tenn
routes.text: The duchy's river, from the castle crag down to the harbour. Barges go down on the current and are hauled back by oxen.

roadEvents.text: A carter going the other way calls the news without stopping: a ship in, a price up, a wedding off.
A ribbon on a thorn, new since yesterday. Someone has come this way with something to ask.
Rain comes over the hill all at once. You walk the next mile with your head down.
A ewe on the wrong side of a wall. You put her back. She is not grateful.
The Duke's riders come through at a canter, and the road stands aside for them.
Smoke hangs in the trees from a kiln you cannot see. The burners know you are here.
A spring by the way, cold enough to hurt your teeth.
A wandering priest of Pecutto, already cheerful, offers you the cup and a verse to go with it.
Mist off the water. For a while there is only the path under your feet.
The bargemen sing the same four lines from the castle to the sea.
A heron gets up from the shallows, slow as a man shaking out a cloak.
A drove of cattle fills the road from hedge to hedge. You wait, and eat their dust.

people.name: Hanne Brook
people.title: Farmhand of Ostwick
people.hint: a sunburnt young woman with a hayfork over her shoulder
people.meet: The young woman with the hayfork has been watching you work all week. “You’re not hopeless,” she says at last. “I’m Hanne. Come and have an ale when the light goes.”
talk: Hanne tells you which cows kick, which fields flood and which of the Brook cousins owes her money.
“One day I’ll have my own strip by the river,” Hanne says. “Barley. Nobody tells barley what to do.”

people.name: Jory Pell
people.title: Eel-Catcher of Kesselhaven
people.hint: a gnarled old man mending eel-traps
people.meet: The old eel-man spits, wipes his hand and holds it out. “Jory. Fifty years on this mole. You set a trap like a drunk priest, but you keep at it. I respect that.”
talk: Jory tells you the harbour was twice as deep when he was a boy, and the eels twice as long.
“Never eat an eel you didn’t kill yourself,” Jory says, and will not explain.

people.name: Mechthild Ambrosius
people.title: Poor Scholar of the Collegium
people.hint: an ink-stained woman asleep on a pile of books
people.meet: The ink-stained woman wakes, looks at what you are reading, and corrects your Allorese. “Mechthild. I’m writing a history of everything. Sit down, you’re in my light.”
talk: Mechthild has found a contradiction in the Collegium’s founding charter and is beside herself with joy.
“Nobody reads anymore,” Mechthild sighs, surrounded by four hundred people reading.

people.name: Zanetta Bon
people.title: Gondolier of Marre
people.hint: a gondolier singing as she rows
people.meet: The gondolier rests her oar. “You row like a Luggish barge, but you’re learning. Zanetta. Get in, I’ll show you the canals nobody shows foreigners.”
talk: Zanetta knows which palazzi have secret water-gates, and which families use them for what.
“Every gondolier in Marre is a spy for somebody,” Zanetta says. “I’m a spy for me.”

people.name: Bastian Caro
people.title: Silverer’s Apprentice of the Glass Isles
people.hint: a pale apprentice with silver on his fingertips
people.meet: The apprentice catches your reflection in a half-silvered glass and smiles at it, not at you. “You have a good reflection. I’m Bastian. Don’t tell the masters I spoke to you.”
talk: Bastian swears the Masque mirrors are just very good glass. He swears it a little too quickly.
“The Republic won’t let silverers leave the Isles,” Bastian says. “I’ve never wanted to. Mostly.”

people.name: Momolo Scarpa
people.title: Smuggler of Selino
people.hint: a lean man in a sailor’s cap who never sits with his back to the door
people.meet: The lean man slides onto the bench beside you. “The Cerdans have your description. That makes you interesting. Momolo. I know a boat.”
talk: Momolo knows every channel in the lagoon the customs boats can’t follow.
“Smuggling’s an honest trade,” Momolo says. “It’s the customs that’s the theft.”

people.name: Cateruccia Vio
people.title: Nurse of the Lazaretto
people.hint: a brisk nurse smelling of vinegar and juniper
people.meet: The nurse pushes a cup of vinegar-water at you. “Drink. You’ve been on the wards a week and you’re not dead, so you’re either lucky or careful. I’m Cateruccia. Be careful.”
talk: Cateruccia has nursed through three Pestilences and has a theory about each of them.
“The Prior says it’s seeds too small to see,” Cateruccia says. “I say it’s dirt. We both say wash your hands.”

people.name: Zaneto Brag
people.title: Warehouse Clerk of the Fondaco
people.hint: a neat Marrean with a ledger in each of four languages
people.meet: He closes one ledger on his finger. “Zaneto Brag. I count what comes from home, and I am locked in with it at curfew.”
talk: Zaneto says the compound is Marre with worse weather and better beer.
“They lock the gate from outside,” Zaneto says. “I have never decided who it protects.”

people.name: Kord Nail
people.title: Door-Keeper of the Cellars
people.hint: a big man on a stool by a door, paring his nails with a knife
people.meet: He does not get up. “Kord Nail. You came in by the right stair, so somebody sent you. Keep your hands where I can count them.”
talk: Kord knows every face that has passed his door and what it owed.
“Up there they have the Salt Council,” Kord says. “Down here we are quicker.”

people.name: Walburg Stock
people.title: Vine-Dresser of Aschau
people.hint: a woman tying a vine to its stake with a twist of straw
people.meet: “Mind the ash on your boots,” she says. “Walburg Stock. The Church says the fire is sin. The vines say otherwise.”
talk: Walburg will not say whether she walks the embers, and nobody asks twice.
“Wine and ash,” Walburg says. “You cannot have this town without both.”

people.name: Eckart Clamp
people.title: Charcoal-Burner of the Grauwald
people.hint: a black-faced man watching a smoking mound as if it might run away
people.meet: “Do not stand downwind,” he says. “Eckart Clamp. Five days and nights I sit by each one. A clamp that flames is firewood.”
talk: Eckart sees the verderers and the outlaws both, and tells neither about the other.
“The wood is the Duke's,” Eckart says. “The smoke is mine.”

people.name: Trudel Moss
people.title: Mother Brindl's carrier
people.hint: a sturdy young woman with a basket on her back and mud to the shin
people.meet: “She is by the fire,” she says. “Bring something useful. Trudel Moss. I fetch and carry and do not ask foolish questions.”
talk: Trudel walks to Ostwick and back most days with things wrapped in leaves.
“She taught me three plants in a year,” Trudel says. “I know them very well.”

people.name: Old Henner
people.title: Ribbon-Bearer of the Oaks
people.hint: an old man standing at the edge of the trees with a fistful of ribbons, saying nothing
people.meet: He puts a finger to his lips and leads you out of the ring before he speaks. “Henner. I tie them for those who cannot walk this far.”
talk: Henner has never spoken under the oaks and does not mean to start.
“There is no priest,” Henner says. “That is why people come.”

people.name: Jockel Fell
people.title: Goat-Herd of the High Meadows
people.hint: a wiry man whistling to goats on a slope you would not walk across
people.meet: He whistles, and forty heads turn. “Jockel Fell. If the bells stop, look at the sky. If the goats run, do not look. Run.”
talk: Jockel winters with the stave-carvers and has a rune over his own door he will not explain.
“Storms do not come here,” Jockel says. “They are made here.”

people.name: Ruprecht Load
people.title: Iron-Bearer of the Caves
people.hint: a broad man with a sack of rusted iron on his back, climbing without hurry
people.meet: He sets the sack down with care. “Ruprecht Load. Nails, horseshoes, a ploughshare. The valley sends it. I carry it. They up there do not talk.”
talk: Ruprecht has carried iron up for twenty years and never been inside when the storm came.
“I asked one what they wait for,” Ruprecht says. “He looked at the sky.”

people.name: Kathe Wedge
people.title: Pot-Woman of the Miner's Lamp
people.hint: a woman filling mugs before the men ask
people.meet: “Shift is up,” she says, and the door opens. Later: “Kathe Wedge. I count them in. Some nights the count is short.”
talk: Kathe keeps a slate of what each miner owes and wipes it clean when a shaft takes one.
“They drink like it is the last,” Kathe says. “Sometimes they are right.”

people.name: Harm Sedge
people.title: Eel-Catcher of the Salzmoor
people.hint: a man walking the mud on boards strapped to his feet
people.meet: “Stop there,” he calls. “That ground is not ground. Harm Sedge. Walk where I walked or go back.”
talk: Harm knows the hour of every tide and whose boat was in the coves last night, and volunteers only the first.
“Everyone else drowns,” Harm says. “It is not a saying. It is a count.”

people.name: Jobst Spade
people.title: Digger at Old Vaelis
people.hint: a sunburnt man sieving earth beside a fallen column
people.meet: “Mine,” he says, of a hole. “Jobst Spade. That one is mine too. Dig anywhere else. Not after dark.”
talk: Jobst has found eleven coins, one bronze hand and nothing that would make him stay after sunset.
“I do not know who carries the lights,” Jobst says. “I have decided not to.”

people.name: Notker Latch
people.title: Lamp-Trimmer of the Sanctum
people.hint: a quiet man filling lamps in an empty hall, counting painted doors under his breath
people.meet: “By day there is only me,” he says. “Notker Latch. I fill the lamps. At dusk I leave. What they do then is theirs.”
talk: Notker has counted the painted doors every day and never reached the same number twice.
“Most are shut,” Notker says. “I do not look long at the open ones.”

people.name: Brida Ladle
people.title: Cook of the Ferryman's Inn
people.hint: a red-faced woman stirring a pot big enough to bathe in
people.meet: “Three languages out there,” she says, “and all of them say stew. Brida Ladle. Sit. The ferry will be an hour. It is always an hour.”
talk: Brida hears the news of three realms a week before the Duke does.
“He has opinions about everyone who crossed,” Brida says, of the ferryman. “I have them about him.”

people.name: Brother Florin
people.title: Orchard-Brother of Pomerell
people.hint: a monk on a ladder, reading a number painted on a trunk
people.meet: “Two hundred and six,” he says. “A good bearer. Brother Florin. We know them by number. I also have names for them, which is not allowed.”
talk: Florin grafted a third of the long ranks himself and can taste which tree a pear came from.
“Forty brothers,” Florin says, “and four thousand trees. The trees are less trouble.”

people.name: Zorza Lant
people.title: Wick-Trimmer of the Lantern
people.hint: a woman polishing a mirror the size of a church door, a hand's breadth at a time
people.meet: “Do not breathe on it,” she says. “Zorza Lant. The old man keeps the lamp. I keep the glass. One smear and a ship is on the rocks.”
talk: Zorza has watched three ships break below and trimmed the wick through each.
“The rocks were here first,” Zorza says. “We only argue with them.”

people.name: Bona Sass
people.title: Shell-Gatherer of the Shallows
people.hint: a woman wading between drowned columns with a basket on her head
people.meet: “Low water,” she says. “Come and see the steps. Bona Sass. They go down further than anyone has walked.”
talk: Bona sells shells to the bead-makers and keeps the carved stones she finds to herself.
“Somebody built a stair into the sea,” Bona says. “Or the sea came up the stair.”

people.name: Tadeo Rin
people.title: Listener at the Crucible
people.hint: a thin man lying with his ear to the ground
people.meet: He holds up a hand for quiet, then sits up. “Tadeo Rin. It rings. Strike it there and listen. Like glass. I have been listening nine years.”
talk: Tadeo says the ringing changes with the tide, and that nobody will pay him to find out why.
“The divers bring up statues,” Tadeo says. “I would rather know what the vessel held.”

people.name: Toma Fach
people.title: Porter at the water-gate of Ca' Loredel
people.hint: a broad-backed man carrying a bale up wet steps
people.meet: He sets the bale down on its mark. “Toma Fach. Thoolman cloth, by the smell. Every wall up there has a map on it. I carry what the maps are about.”
talk: Toma can tell what a house is buying by how its barges sit in the water.
“Three palazzi on this bend,” Toma says. “I am welcome at the back of one.”

people.name: Zulian Risi
people.title: Rice-Hand of the Terraferma
people.hint: a man bent double in a flooded field, with herons standing closer than he likes
people.meet: He straightens, slowly. “Zulian Risi. Water to the knee from spring to harvest. The Families see this from a portico.”
talk: Zulian says the mosquitoes sing all night and he has stopped hearing them, which worries his wife.
“White villas, green fields,” Zulian says. “It looks well from a boat.”

people.name: Menega Gomm
people.title: Mastic-Gatherer of Morena
people.hint: a woman scraping pale beads of resin from a scored trunk
people.meet: “Do not step on the tears,” she says. “Menega Gomm. The trees weep, we gather, both empires chew it. Nobody asks the trees.”
talk: Menega sells to the Fondaco and says the Thoolman quarter pays better and the castle must not know.
“Half-way to everywhere,” Menega says. “That is what an island is for.”

people.name: Gerd Sack
people.title: Miller of Weirbeck
people.hint: a floury man with one shoulder higher than the other
people.meet: The miller looks at your hands before your face. “You can lift,” he says. “Good. I'm Gerd. Mind the stones.”
talk: Gerd tells you which farmers bring damp corn and hope he will not notice.
“A mill takes a sixteenth,” Gerd says. “Anyone who says I take more can turn the wheel himself.”

people.name: Alder Finch
people.title: Hayward of Netherwick
people.hint: a lean man walking the hedge with a billhook, counting gaps
people.meet: “Mind the gate,” says the man with the billhook, before anything else. Then, when you have minded it: “Alder Finch. Hayward. That means the hedges are my fault.”
talk: Alder can tell you whose cow got into whose corn, in what year, and what it cost.
“Hedges are law you can see,” Alder says.

people.name: Wilmar Tally
people.title: Clerk of the Tithe
people.hint: a neat young man with ink on his cuffs and a notched stick behind his ear
people.meet: “Name and holding,” says the clerk, without looking up. When you have neither, he looks up. “Wilmar. I count what is owed.”
talk: Wilmar explains the split tally: one half for the tenant, one for the Duke, and no arguing with wood.
“Everyone thinks the tenth is the sheaf I take,” Wilmar says. “It is the nine I leave.”

people.name: Old Nell Crook
people.title: Shepherd of the Common
people.hint: an old woman knitting as she walks, with two dogs that watch you instead of the sheep
people.meet: The old woman finishes her row before she speaks. “You'll be the new one. Nell. The dogs are Bit and Bother. Don't feed Bother.”
talk: Nell knows every ewe on the common by its face and most by its mother's.
“Sit facing the stone,” Nell says. “Never mind why. Your grandmother would have known.”

people.name: Lise Marsh
people.title: Goose-Girl of Dunmere
people.hint: a young woman with a long switch and a flock that goes where she looks
people.meet: The geese reach you before she does. “They don't bite,” says the girl with the switch. “Well. That one bites. I'm Lise.”
talk: Lise drives forty geese to the castle kitchens every week and comes home with thirty-nine fewer.
“Geese know who is afraid of them,” Lise says. “So do I.”

people.name: Hob Wade
people.title: Keeper of the Ford
people.hint: a broad man standing in the water as if it were a road
people.meet: “Wait,” says the man in the water, and you wait while he reads the beck. “Now.” On the far side: “Hob. I say when.”
talk: Hob has pulled eleven carts, two friars and a bull out of the beck, and remembers the bull best.
“Water tells you everything,” Hob says, “just before it is too late.”

people.name: Berta Ash
people.title: Hearth-Keeper of the Cross
people.hint: a woman with soot to the elbows, feeding a fire one stick at a time
people.meet: She takes your stick, looks it over and lays it on. “Dry. Good. I'm Berta. The fire is older than the road.”
talk: Berta walks to the Ostwick shrine each week and carries a coal back in a clay pot.
“People think a hearth is kept by wood,” Berta says. “It is kept by coming back.”

people.name: Tom Russet
people.title: Picker of Sallowfield
people.hint: a long-armed man who looks at trees the way other men look at horses
people.meet: “That one will crop heavy,” says the long-armed man, nodding at a tree. Then at you: “Tom. You pick?”
talk: Tom knows the abbey's trees by their numbers and disagrees with the brothers about four of them.
“A ladder is only as good as its foot,” Tom says.

people.name: Kunz Hemp
people.title: The Duke's Hangman
people.hint: a quiet man mending a rope with a sailmaker's care
people.meet: He does not offer a hand. “Folk would rather not,” he says. “Kunz. I am paid by the Duke and thanked by nobody.”
talk: Kunz says a good knot is a kindness, and that he has never yet been asked what he thinks of a sentence.
“They cross the road to miss me,” Kunz says. “Then they send for me when a tooth wants pulling.”

people.name: Anke Dorn
people.title: Laundress to the Castle
people.hint: a red-armed woman who can tell a knight by his shirts
people.meet: “Whose are you?” she asks, and when you are nobody's: “Then you can carry. Anke. Those are the Duke's. Don't drop them.”
talk: Anke knows which knights are in debt, which are in love and which are ill, all from the linen.
“There are no secrets in a castle,” Anke says. “There is only washing.”

people.name: Dirk Hale
people.title: Host of the Broken Lance
people.hint: a grey man with a sergeant's voice and a limp he does not discuss
people.meet: “Sit,” says the host, in a voice that has moved pikemen. You sit. “Dirk. Served the Duke twenty years. Now I serve his squires, which is worse.”
talk: Dirk will tell you who unhorsed whom at any tourney for thirty years, and why it was the horse's fault.
“The lance over the fire is mine,” Dirk says. “The man who broke it paid for the inn.”

people.name: Jutta Lark
people.title: Lure-Maker of Falkenau
people.hint: a small woman stitching a leather lure, with a hawk asleep on the chair-back
people.meet: “Don't look her in the eye,” says the woman with the needle, meaning the hawk. “Jutta. She is Thistle. She is in a mood.”
talk: Jutta makes lures for the ducal mews and can tell you which of the Duke's birds will never be any good.
“A hawk does not love you,” Jutta says. “She agrees with you. For now.”

people.name: Bruno Slate
people.title: Quarryman
people.hint: a man the colour of his stone, with a maul over his shoulder
people.meet: He raps the rock and listens. “Sound,” he says, to the rock, and then to you: “Bruno. Stand there. Not there.”
talk: Bruno's grandfather cut the keep's gate-arch and was paid, the family says, in promises.
“Stone splits where it wants,” Bruno says. “The craft is in wanting the same.”

people.name: Mats Cole
people.title: Charcoal Carter
people.hint: a man black to the eyes, leading an ox that is black to the knees
people.meet: White teeth in a black face. “Don't shake hands,” he says. “Mats. You'll want to stand upwind.”
talk: Mats carries charcoal to the Silberhalde smelters and news back, and charges for neither.
“The forest burns slow or it burns fast,” Mats says. “We are the slow.”

people.name: Hilde Bracken
people.title: Forester of the Grauwald
people.hint: a woman in green and grey who was standing there some time before you saw her
people.meet: “You walk loud,” she says, from much nearer than you thought. “Hilde. The Duke's forester. That was not a complaint. It was a warning.”
talk: Hilde keeps the deer-count in her head and the roll only for the Duke's clerks.
“Poachers I can forgive,” Hilde says. “It is the ones who leave the snare that I hang.”

people.name: Wat Rush
people.title: Reed-Cutter
people.hint: a man in a punt, cutting without looking, with a pipe that is not lit
people.meet: The punt noses in. “Step in the middle,” he says, “or step in the mere.” When you are aboard: “Wat. I thatch half of Ostwick.”
talk: Wat sells thatch to the village and eels to the miller, and will not say what he sells to Mother Brindl.
“Reed grows back,” Wat says. “That is the whole of what I know, and it has fed me fifty years.”

people.name: Else Fold
people.title: Shearer of Steinwick
people.hint: a woman with forearms like a smith, sharpening shears on her boot
people.meet: “Hold that,” she says, and gives you a ewe. When the ewe has made its views known: “Else. You held on. That'll do.”
talk: Else can shear a ewe while it is still deciding whether to object.
“Wool is the only crop that walks to market,” Else says.

people.name: Henk Stave
people.title: Cooper
people.hint: a cheerful man rolling a cask with one foot while he talks
people.meet: The cask rolls up to your feet and stops. “Good, you can catch,” says the cooper. “Henk. That one leaks. Tell me where.”
talk: Henk makes the casks for Aschau's wine and says the wine is only as honest as the wood.
“A cask is a hundred mistakes you did not make,” Henk says.

people.name: Brother Otmar
people.title: Granger of Pomerell
people.hint: a monk with his sleeves tied back, talking to an ox as to a novice
people.meet: “He is called Patience,” says the monk, of the ox. “He is not. I am Brother Otmar, and I am learning it from him.”
talk: Brother Otmar keeps the grange accounts in the same book as the apple-trees, a page to each ox.
“The abbot prays for rain,” Otmar says. “I mend the roof.”

people.name: Old Rolf
people.title: Beacon-Ward
people.hint: an old soldier asleep sitting up, with one eye that opens before the other
people.meet: One eye opens. “I was not asleep,” says the old man. “I was listening. Rolf. I have lit that fire twice, and I would rather not a third time.”
talk: Rolf was a levy spearman and will show you the scar, whether or not you ask.
“A beacon is the Duke saying please,” Rolf says. “Loudly.”

people.name: Jost Marsh
people.title: Toll-Clerk of the Salters' Gate
people.hint: a young man counting carts aloud without moving his lips
people.meet: “Forty-one,” he says, to nobody. Then, to you: “Jost Marsh. Do not speak to me while a cart is under the arch.”
talk: Jost knows which carters water their salt, and charges them by the wet weight.
“Salt goes out, silver comes in,” Jost says. “I am the hinge.”

people.name: Wiebke Tarn
people.title: Netmender of the Strand
people.hint: a woman with a bone needle in her teeth and a net over her knees
people.meet: She speaks round the needle. “Wiebke Tarn. Hold that end. No, the other end.”
talk: Wiebke can tell which boat a net came off by the knots.
“A fish only needs one hole,” Wiebke says. “I need to find all of them.”

people.name: Anselm Hoop
people.title: Cooper of the Yard
people.hint: a thick-armed man knocking a hoop down with a mallet
people.meet: He finishes the hoop first. “Anselm Hoop. And yes, that is the name, and no, I did not choose the trade to fit it.”
talk: Anselm says a good barrel is tight without glue or nails, and so is a good guild.
“Everything in this town travels in my work,” Anselm says. “Nobody looks at the barrel.”

people.name: Frauke Fenn
people.title: Eel-Smoker of Eelwater
people.hint: a woman with smoke-red eyes and a string of eels over her shoulder
people.meet: “Shut the door,” she says. “The smoke is the money.” Then: “Frauke Fenn. You get used to it.”
talk: Frauke sells half her catch in the market and the other half, she says, to people who do not use the market.
“Alder, not oak,” Frauke says. “Oak is for people who do not like eels.”

people.name: Konrad Vellum
people.title: Bookseller of the Row
people.hint: a dusty man reading his own stock with a finger on the line
people.meet: He keeps his finger where it is. “Konrad Vellum. You may read standing up for nothing. Sitting down costs.”
talk: Konrad buys the same books back from the same students every spring.
“A scholar sells his books in this order,” Konrad says. “Theology first. Then the rest.”

people.name: Lena Hale
people.title: Shepherd of Starwatch
people.hint: a young woman with a crook, scratching numbers on a slate
people.meet: “They pay me to keep the sheep off the stones,” she says. “Lena Hale. I learned the rest by listening.”
talk: Lena can name more stars than most of the students who climb the hill.
“The sheep do not care which way is north,” Lena says. “I do, now.”

people.name: Ebbo Rake
people.title: Salt-Panner of the Row
people.hint: a man with cracked hands and a wide wooden rake
people.meet: He shows you his palms. “Ebbo Rake. That is what salt does. Still better than the mines.”
talk: Ebbo says the moor gives salt to anyone and takes a cart, a horse or a man every few years in exchange.
“Wind and sun do the work,” Ebbo says. “I only tidy up after them.”

people.name: Brother Ansgar
people.title: Keeper of the Mud Chapel
people.hint: a monk with his habit tucked up and mud to the knee
people.meet: “Boots off,” he says. “The floor is the cleanest thing for a mile.” Then: “Brother Ansgar. I ring the bell and I cut the names.”
talk: Ansgar has pulled eleven people off the flats by following his own bell back.
“The tide keeps no hours you can trust,” Ansgar says. “So I keep mine.”

people.name: Greta Stile
people.title: Farmer of Haverford
people.hint: a brisk woman with a sack of oats on one hip
people.meet: “If you are going to the moor, you are going the wrong way,” she says. “Greta Stile. Everyone asks.”
talk: Greta charges carters for oats and for pulling them out of the ford, and says the second pays better.
“A horse works on oats,” Greta says. “So this town works on me.”

people.name: Dierk Tow
people.title: Hauler of the Reach
people.hint: a broad man leaning into a rope as if into a wind
people.meet: He does not stop. “Walk with me if you want to talk. Dierk Tow. The barge will not wait.”
talk: Dierk has walked from the sea to the ferry more times than he can count, and never once back by water.
“Downstream is free,” Dierk says. “Upstream is me.”

people.name: Gesche Retter
people.title: Flax-Wife of Osterau
people.hint: a tall woman beating a bundle of flax as if it had insulted her
people.meet: She gives it one more blow. “Gesche Retter. You will stop noticing the smell in a day. Or a year.”
talk: Gesche sells her best line to the Fondaco and says they pay in promises and thin silver.
“Linen is patience you can wear,” Gesche says.

people.name: Rupp Halter
people.title: Horse-Coper of Lindenau
people.hint: a bow-legged man looking at a horse’s teeth
people.meet: He lets the lip go. “Seven, not five. Rupp Halter. Never buy a horse from a man in a hurry.”
talk: Rupp remembers every horse he has sold and what became of it.
“The knights want height,” Rupp says. “The carters want sense. I breed for the carters.”

people.name: Detlef Clink
people.title: Picker of the Heaps
people.hint: a young man with a hammer, cracking stones and looking inside
people.meet: He cracks one more. “Nothing. Detlef Clink. One in fifty has colour in it.”
talk: Detlef sells what he finds back to the smelter that threw it away.
“They are in a hurry up there,” Detlef says. “I am not.”

people.name: Marta Pick
people.title: Washerwoman of Stollenwick
people.hint: a woman wringing a grey shirt over a grey trough
people.meet: “Do not lean on that wall, it is drying,” she says. “Marta Pick. Three sons below. I count them up every night.”
talk: Marta knows which seam is being worked by the colour of the dirt that comes home.
“Silver comes out white,” Marta says. “Everything else comes out grey.”

people.name: Gunther Snare
people.title: Wolf-Warden of the Pits
people.hint: a quiet man with a spear and a limp
people.meet: “Walk where I walk,” he says. “Exactly.” When you are across: “Gunther Snare. That is how I got the limp.”
talk: Gunther has taken four wolves in nine years, and says the pits mostly catch drunkards.
“The wolves know where the pits are,” Gunther says. “That is the point.”

people.name: Irmel Horn
people.title: Herdswoman of the High Byre
people.hint: a sunburnt woman with a cow-horn slung on a cord
people.meet: She blows one note on the horn and every cow looks up. “Irmel Horn. That is all the magic I have.”
talk: Irmel has not been below the tree-line between thaw and frost since she was twelve.
“Up here the weather tells you first,” Irmel says. “Down there you find out.”

people.name: Odila Staff
people.title: Sweeper of the Stair
people.hint: an old woman with a birch broom, working downward
people.meet: “Mind the wet ones,” she says. “Odila Staff. My mother swept it. Do not ask me why. It wants sweeping.”
talk: Odila says you can tell a pilgrim from a scholar by which of them looks at the steps.
“Going up, they pray,” Odila says. “Coming down, they are hungry.”

people.name: Lutz Tread
people.title: Pressman of Kelterwick
people.hint: a man with purple feet and a contented look
people.meet: He looks down at his feet with you. “Lutz Tread. They go white again by spring.”
talk: Lutz can tell the slope a grape grew on by treading it.
“The press does the work,” Lutz says. “The feet do the first kindness.”

people.name: Sanne Withy
people.title: Ford-Keeper of Appleford
people.hint: a young woman with a pole, standing in the stream to her knees
people.meet: “Left of the white stone,” she calls. “Left!” Then, wading out: “Sanne Withy. They never listen the first time.”
talk: Sanne has fished nine barrels and one abbot out of the ford.
“The river is polite in summer,” Sanne says. “Do not trust it.”

people.name: Brother Emmeran
people.title: Bee-Ward of the Garth
people.hint: a monk walking slowly along a wall, talking under his breath
people.meet: He holds up a finger until he has finished the sentence. “I was telling them the news. Brother Emmeran. They like to know.”
talk: Emmeran says the bees are told of every death at the abbey before the bell is rung.
“No orchard without them,” Emmeran says. “The abbot knows it, too.”

people.name: Wendel Sluice
people.title: Weir-Keeper of Greywater
people.hint: a wet man lifting a wicker trap and peering in
people.meet: “Trout,” he says, pleased, and then sees you. “Wendel Sluice. The Duke gets every third one. I choose which.”
talk: Wendel clears the weir after every storm and finds something odd in it each time.
“Water wants to go round,” Wendel says. “My whole trade is saying no.”

people.name: Ortwin Peat
people.title: Turf-Cutter of Brackenfell
people.hint: a stooped man with a long narrow spade
people.meet: “Step on the brown, not the green,” he says. “Ortwin Peat. The green is water with a skin on.”
talk: Ortwin once cut a pair of boots out of the moor, a thousand years old and better made than his.
“It burns slow and it burns all night,” Ortwin says. “Like a grudge.”

people.name: Mother Gundel
people.title: Keeper of the Sisters
people.hint: an old woman untying faded rags and tying on fresh ones
people.meet: “Do not walk between them,” she says, not unkindly. “Round. Mother Gundel. I keep count of the wishes.”
talk: Mother Gundel says the stones lean a finger further each year, toward each other.
“People ask them for small things,” she says. “That is why it works.”

people.name: Falk Scree
people.title: Guide of the Pass
people.hint: a lean man watching a cloud as if it had spoken
people.meet: “Not today,” he says, before you ask. “Falk Scree. Tomorrow before noon, or not at all.”
talk: Falk leaves firewood in the shelter every autumn and has never found out who uses it.
“The mountain does not hate you,” Falk says. “It has not noticed you.”

people.name: Imke Spile
people.title: Alewife of the Antler
people.hint: a red-armed woman carrying four mugs in each hand
people.meet: She puts eight mugs down without spilling. “Imke Spile. Sit anywhere that is not under the big one. It falls.”
talk: Imke settles every argument about who shot what by pointing at the wall.
“Foresters drink like men who work alone,” Imke says. “All at once.”

people.name: Tilo Wand
people.title: Basket-Maker of Mossbeck
people.hint: a man weaving without looking at his hands
people.meet: His hands keep going. “Tilo Wand. Ask me anything. They do not need me for this part.”
talk: Tilo makes a cradle for every child born in the village and a creel for every man who dies.
“Willow forgives,” Tilo says. “Oak holds a grudge.”

people.name: Arno Axle
people.title: Wheelwright of Silverford
people.hint: a man rolling a wheel along with one finger
people.meet: He lets the wheel lean against you. “Hold that. Arno Axle. An ore cart breaks here every day. I thank the Duke’s roads.”
talk: Arno can tell a carter’s temper from the wear on his wheels.
“Round is easy,” Arno says. “Round and true is the trade.”

people.name: Veit Grist
people.title: Miller of the Burgmill
people.hint: a man with flour in his eyebrows and a short measure in his hand
people.meet: “Castle corn first,” he says. “Then yours. Veit Grist. I did not make the law, I only like it.”
talk: Veit knows the size of every holding on the demesne by the sacks that come from it.
“They must come here,” Veit says. “So I need not be pleasant.”

people.name: Wolfram Ember
people.title: Beacon-Keeper of Rabenstein
people.hint: a grey man feeding a raven from his hand
people.meet: “He bites,” he says, as the raven does not. “Wolfram Ember. I have kept this fire ready thirty years and lit it once.”
talk: Wolfram will not say what the once was for.
“A beacon is a promise,” Wolfram says. “Mostly you keep it by doing nothing.”

people.name: Elke Roe
people.title: Fisher of Nordwick
people.hint: a woman knee-deep in the river with a hand-net
people.meet: “Stand still,” she says. “You are frightening my supper.” Later: “Elke Roe. They only run a fortnight. Then we wait.”
talk: Elke says the salmon come back to the very gravel they were born on, and that people are the same.
“You cannot hurry the run,” Elke says. “You can only be here.”

people.name: Udo Winch
people.title: Chainman of the Ferry
people.hint: a thick-necked man leaning on a capstan bar
people.meet: “When the horn goes, push,” he says. “Udo Winch. When it goes twice, push harder.”
talk: Udo has crossed the river ten thousand times and never been to the other side’s village.
“The ferryman takes the coin,” Udo says. “I take the river.”

people.name: Kai Lead
people.title: Pilot of Sandhaven
people.hint: a man squinting at a sail nobody else can see yet
people.meet: “Marrean,” he says, of a speck. “Deep-laden. Kai Lead. First boat out gets the fee.”
talk: Kai knows the bar the way Ostwick farmers know their strips.
“The sand moves every storm,” Kai says. “The charts are a year behind. I am not.”

people.name: Rike Kettle
people.title: Tar-Boiler of the Kilns
people.hint: a woman black to the elbow, stirring with a paddle
people.meet: “Do not touch anything,” she says. “Including me. Rike Kettle.”
talk: Rike says every ship out of Kesselhaven floats on her work and smells of it too.
“Tar keeps the sea out,” Rike says. “And company.”

people.name: Meta Scale
people.title: Fish-Seller of the Stairs
people.hint: a woman shouting a price and dropping it as she shouts
people.meet: “Six! Five and a half!” She looks at you. “Meta Scale. Four to you if you take the barrel.”
talk: Meta says the price of herring is whatever the last boat in will take.
“By noon it is cat-food,” Meta says. “So I talk fast.”

people.name: Volker Wick
people.title: Night-Watchman of the Court
people.hint: a heavy man lighting a lantern from another lantern
people.meet: “Curfew is for other people,” he says. “You are other people. Volker Wick.”
talk: Volker knows which doors in the Undercroft to knock on and which to walk past.
“I am paid to be seen,” Volker says. “Catching anyone is extra.”

people.name: Ilse White
people.title: Bleacher of the Fields
people.hint: a woman sprinkling a strip of linen from a can
people.meet: “Mind the cloth!” Then, calmer: “Ilse White. Sun, water and time. And no boots.”
talk: Ilse can tell Osterau linen from any other by how fast it whitens.
“Six weeks to turn it white,” Ilse says. “One muddy dog to turn it back.”

people.name: Jorg Bine
people.title: Hop-Grower of Mittelau
people.hint: a man on stilts tying a string to the top of a pole
people.meet: He looks down. “Jorg Bine. Yes, stilts. You try reaching it.”
talk: Jorg says the brewers of Kesselhaven would be selling sweet barley-water without him.
“Ale is my hops and somebody else’s credit,” Jorg says.

people.name: Regine Prune
people.title: Vine-Dresser of Sonnhalde
people.hint: a woman with a curved knife, cutting more off a vine than she leaves
people.meet: “It looks cruel,” she says, cutting. “Regine Prune. A vine left alone makes leaves. I want grapes.”
talk: Regine rebuilds a stretch of wall every winter and says the hill is trying to lie down.
“Poor soil, good wine,” Regine says. “It is the only thing poor soil is good for.”

people.name: Hanno Reed
people.title: Reed-Cutter of Southmere
people.hint: a man in a flat boat, cutting below the waterline with a long hook
people.meet: “Winter work,” he says. “When the leaf is off. Hanno Reed. You have come at the right time or the wrong one.”
talk: Hanno says a good reed roof outlasts the man who laid it and the man who paid.
“Straw is for barns,” Hanno says.

people.name: Brother Wido
people.title: Recluse of the Red Scar
people.hint: a thin man lowering a basket on a rope, very slowly
people.meet: A voice from above: “If it is advice, I have none. If it is bread, thank you. Brother Wido.”
talk: Wido came up for a week of quiet, eleven years ago.
“I do not dislike people,” Wido says. “I like them better from here.”

people.name: Benno Bar
people.title: Border-Rider of the Westmark
people.hint: a rider asleep in the saddle, on a horse that is wide awake
people.meet: The horse nudges him. “Hm. Benno Bar. Anything to declare? No? Good. I hate the ledger.”
talk: Benno says more goes round the stone than past it, and that he is not paid enough to mind.
“The Duchy stops here,” Benno says. “The mud keeps going.”

people.name: Ludolf von Ehrenau
people.title: Seneschal of Burg Tennfels
people.hint: a tall, tired man with a ring of keys he never puts down
people.meet: He counts you as he would a delivery. “Ludolf von Ehrenau. I keep the Duke's house. You will find that it keeps you.”
talk: Ludolf has served the Salt-Duke since before the Duke was gouty, and will not say which he preferred.
“A house is run on what nobody notices,” Ludolf says. “The day they notice, you have failed.”

people.name: Adelheid Korn
people.title: Housekeeper of Burg Tennfels
people.hint: a brisk woman counting linen aloud and losing her place when you come in
people.meet: “Forty-one. Forty… you have made me lose it.” She looks you up and down. “Adelheid Korn. If you are staying, you can count.”
talk: Adelheid knows which maids can be trusted with the Heiress's rooms, and it is fewer than you would hope.
“The seneschal has the keys,” Adelheid says. “I have the doors.”

people.name: Bodo Rind
people.title: Cook to the Duke
people.hint: a vast man in a scorched apron, shouting at a pot
people.meet: The pot has done something wrong. So, it seems, have you. “Out of my light! … Bodo. Cook. Taste that. No, with the other spoon.”
talk: Bodo cooks for the Duke's gout, the legate's conscience and sixty hungry men-at-arms, from one fire.
“They send it back if it is cold,” Bodo says. “They send it back if it is hot. I have stopped listening.”

people.name: Master Reinhild Stark
people.title: Master of the Guild Forges
people.hint: a square-built woman who tests each bar by ringing it on the anvil
people.meet: She rings a bar on the anvil and listens. “Hear that? No. You will.” She holds out a hand like a vice. “Reinhild Stark. If you waste my iron I will know.”
talk: Reinhild says the guild keeps three rules: fair weight, true temper, and no selling to the Rats.
“Anyone can make a thing hot,” Reinhild says. “The craft is in when you stop.”

people.name: Till Ember
people.title: Journeyman of the Anvil
people.hint: a young smith with burn-scars to the elbow, watching your hammer-hand
people.meet: “You hold it like a spoon,” says the young smith. He shows you. “Till. I was worse. Not much worse.”
talk: Till means to walk his journeyman years in Luggen, where they pay by the piece.
“Reinhild failed my first piece,” Till says. “She was right. Do not tell her.”

people.name: Tonina Sgarb
people.title: Scrivener of the Calle
people.hint: a woman with a black thumb and a pen behind each ear
people.meet: She blots the line before she looks up. “Tonina Sgarb. I copy what I am given and forget it by supper. That is the trade.”
talk: Tonina can tell a clerk of the Council from a clerk of the Cerdans by the paper they bring.
“A fair hand is worth more than a fair face here,” Tonina says. “Faces change at Carnevale.”

people.name: Bortolo Pes
people.title: Measurer of Grain
people.hint: a broad man with chaff in his beard and a tally-board on a cord
people.meet: “Stand off the plank,” he says, and then, when the sack has passed: “Bortolo Pes. I measure. The Republic believes me, so the bargemen must.”
talk: Bortolo says the barges ride lower in a good year, and that he can read the harvest from the bridge.
“Level measure,” Bortolo says. “Not heaped, not shaken. Level.”

people.name: Marietta Zan
people.title: Lion-Keeper of the Matron
people.hint: an old woman polishing a stone lion with her sleeve
people.meet: “Rub his nose,” she says. “This one you may.” She watches you do it. “Marietta Zan. I keep the glass ones. These keep me.”
talk: Marietta has dusted the sleeping lion every morning for forty years and says he has never once stirred.
“One awake, one asleep,” Marietta says. “That is how to run a city.”

people.name: Nane Tosat
people.title: Boatman of the Riva
people.hint: a boatman resting on his oar with his cap over his eyes
people.meet: He lifts the cap an inch. “Nane Tosat. I carry bread in and letters out. I do not read either.”
talk: Nane knows which families have been waiting a week and which a year, by where they moor.
“In summer the roof is the punishment,” Nane says. “The judge only chooses how long.”

people.name: Catina Fol
people.title: Keeper of the Bauta
people.hint: a woman who fills your cup without asking and listens without seeming to
people.meet: She sets the cup down. “Catina Fol. Drink, pay, and talk about the weather. Everyone here does.”
talk: Catina can tell who is watching whom by which bench they choose.
“I hear nothing,” Catina says. “I am paid twice for it.”

people.name: Menego Rui
people.title: Boatwright of the Squero
people.hint: a man sighting along a plank with one eye shut
people.meet: “Crooked,” he says, pleased, and puts the plank down. “Menego Rui. If it were straight it would go in circles.”
talk: Menego builds one boat in a season and says the Arsenal builds a galley a day because nobody has to love a galley.
“Eight woods in a gondola,” Menego says. “And one man’s temper.”

people.name: Betta Guss
people.title: Fishwife of the Pescaria
people.hint: a woman gutting sardines faster than you can count them
people.meet: “Fresh,” she says, before you ask. “Betta Guss. If it winks at you it is too fresh.”
talk: Betta knows which cook buys for which palazzo, and what each house is eating less of this month.
“The Ten Families eat what I say is good,” Betta says. “They think their cooks choose.”

people.name: Zuane Tinto
people.title: Dyer of the Corte
people.hint: a man whose hands are blue to the wrist and red above it
people.meet: He holds up both hands. “Zuane Tinto. Do not shake them. It does not come off.”
talk: Zuane will not say which house’s colour is hardest to match, only that one of them never pays on time.
“Every house has a colour,” Zuane says. “I am the only man in Marre who wears them all.”

people.name: Lucieta Bas
people.title: Mask-Maker of the Ponte
people.hint: a young woman painting a white mask with a brush of three hairs
people.meet: “Hold still,” she says, and measures your face with her thumb. “Lucieta Bas. You would suit a plain one. Most people do.”
talk: Lucieta remembers every face she has fitted, which is more than her customers would like.
“By law nobody may ask who you are in a mask,” Lucieta says. “Nobody said I could not know.”

people.name: Anzolo Fri
people.title: Mirror-Dealer of the Fondamenta
people.hint: a thin man who looks at your reflection instead of at you
people.meet: He speaks to the glass. “Anzolo Fri. Every mirror here is honest. That is why they are dear.”
talk: Anzolo can name the master of any mirror by the colour of its silver.
“A cheap mirror flatters,” Anzolo says. “Ours do not, and people pay for it. Explain that.”

people.name: Stae Dolfi
people.title: Oarsman of the Health Boat
people.hint: a sunburnt man who keeps an oar’s length from everyone
people.meet: He holds up a hand before you come closer. “Stae Dolfi. I row the officers round. Stay upwind and we shall get on.”
talk: Stae counts days for forty ships at once and has never been wrong by one.
“Day thirty-nine is the long one,” Stae says.

people.name: Tita Nard
people.title: Corpse-Bearer of the Quiet Isle
people.hint: a big, gentle man with lime on his boots and a ledger under his arm
people.meet: He takes off his cap. “Tita Nard. I write them all down. Somebody comes asking, in the end.”
talk: Tita says the island is the only place in the lagoon where nobody lies to him.
“A name and a day,” Tita says. “It is not much. It is more than the sea gives.”

people.name: Agnesina Rov
people.title: Herb-Wife of the Simples
people.hint: a small woman in a straw hat, crushing a leaf under your nose
people.meet: “Smell,” she says. “Now you will not forget it. Agnesina Rov. Half of physic is not picking the wrong one.”
talk: Agnesina sends a basket to the wards every dawn and gets it back empty every dusk.
“The fever-bark comes from across the sea,” Agnesina says. “Everything else comes from me.”

people.name: Checo Bisat
people.title: Eel-Man of the Shallows
people.hint: a wiry man hauling a wicker trap hand over hand
people.meet: “Wet feet,” he says, looking at yours. “Checo Bisat. Sit on the dry side. There is one.”
talk: Checo knows the lagoon’s channels by the colour of the water and has never owned a chart.
“The city thinks the lagoon is its moat,” Checo says. “It is its larder.”

people.name: Iseppo Lanz
people.title: Pilot of the Bar
people.hint: a grey man watching the water as if it owed him money
people.meet: He does not turn round. “Iseppo Lanz. The bar moved a boat’s length last winter. Nobody told the charts.”
talk: Iseppo has brought in every spice-galley for twenty autumns and says they ride lower each year.
“A foreign captain asks how deep,” Iseppo says. “A wise one asks me to take the helm.”

people.name: Gasparo Ton
people.title: Barge-Master of the Stair
people.hint: a heavy man shouting at a barge as if it could hear
people.meet: He stops shouting to look you over. “Gasparo Ton. If it floats and it is slow, it is mine.”
talk: Gasparo says the city would starve in a week without his barges and has said so to a senator.
“Glass goes out on galleys,” Gasparo says. “Supper comes in on me.”

people.name: Orsetta Brun
people.title: Silk-Wife of the Sheds
people.hint: a woman carrying a tray of leaves as if it were asleep
people.meet: “Softly,” she says. “They can hear you.” She sets the tray down. “Orsetta Brun. No shouting, no smoke, no thunder if you can help it.”
talk: Orsetta has not slept a whole night in silk season since she was a girl.
“The city wears it,” Orsetta says. “We raise it. Ask which is harder.”

people.name: Bepi Sguaz
people.title: Keeper of the Chiusa
people.hint: a man in mud to the knee with a heron standing beside him
people.meet: “Mind the heron,” he says. “He was here first. Bepi Sguaz. I let the water in and I let it out.”
talk: Bepi is offered a bribe by every farmer each spring and takes them all, in order.
“Water is patient,” Bepi says. “Farmers are not. I stand between.”

people.name: Nineta Scoa
people.title: Cullet-Picker of Ash Isle
people.hint: a young woman with rag-bound hands and a sack that clinks
people.meet: She shakes the sack at you. “Nineta Scoa. Do not pick anything up. You will bleed, and then you will know why.”
talk: Nineta can tell which furnace a shard came from by its green.
“They burn it, they break it, they buy it back,” Nineta says. “I am the only one who gets paid twice.”

people.name: Vettor Stagn
people.title: Captain of the Guard Boats
people.hint: a patient man counting lit windows on the far shore
people.meet: He finishes counting first. “Vettor Stagn. Every master is at his furnace tonight. That is all I am asked.”
talk: Vettor has rowed round the Isles for eleven years and knows every glassmaker by his silhouette.
“They are the richest prisoners in the world,” Vettor says. “I am the poorest gaoler.”

people.name: Pasqua Forn
people.title: Baker of the Ovens
people.hint: a floury woman knocking two biscuits together and listening
people.meet: “Hear that?” she says. “That will last to the spice-coasts. Pasqua Forn. Do not try to eat one dry.”
talk: Pasqua says a galley rows on her biscuit and complains about it the whole way.
“Twice baked,” Pasqua says. “Once for the weevils, once for the sea.”

people.name: Tofolo Secc
people.title: Water-Seller of the Stairs
people.hint: a man with a dipper on a chain, tasting before he sells
people.meet: He sips, nods, and holds out the dipper. “Tofolo Secc. Taste it now. In a month at sea you will dream of it.”
talk: Tofolo can tell which cistern a cup came from, and which captain watered his crew from the cheap one.
“Gold buys spice,” Tofolo says. “Water buys coming home.”

people.name: Jacomo Bolz
people.title: Drill-Master of the Yard
people.hint: a scarred man winding a crossbow without looking at it
people.meet: “Feet apart,” he says. “Wider. Jacomo Bolz. The sea will not hold still for you, so learn not to need it.”
talk: Jacomo has made the run east nine times and counts that as nine times lucky.
“Anyone can hit a man on land,” Jacomo says.

people.name: Sabina Pegn
people.title: Pawnbroker of the Arch
people.hint: a woman weighing a ring and the man who brought it, both at a glance
people.meet: “Two months,” she says, to the ring. Then to you: “Sabina Pegn. I do not buy. I keep.”
talk: Sabina has coats in the loft whose owners sailed ten autumns ago, and will not sell them.
“They all mean to come back for it,” Sabina says.

people.name: Bettina Spiz
people.title: Watcher of the Lookout
people.hint: a woman in a shawl, knitting without looking down from the horizon
people.meet: “Sit,” she says. “It is a long watch. Bettina Spiz. I count sails in and I count sails out.”
talk: Bettina has been right about every overdue galley for twenty years, and wishes she were not.
“Low in the water is good news,” Bettina says. “It means they found something to carry.”

people.name: Zorzi Rasp
people.title: Scraper of the Hard
people.hint: a man with a long iron scraper and a face full of flakes
people.meet: “Mind the tallow,” he says. “Zorzi Rasp. A clean hull is a week sooner home.”
talk: Zorzi can tell which sea a galley has been in by what is growing on her.
“Nobody thanks the man underneath,” Zorzi says.

people.name: Nadalin Forcol
people.title: Oar-Maker of the Campo
people.hint: a man balancing an oar on one finger
people.meet: It tips, and he shaves a curl off. “Nadalin Forcol. Too heavy by that much. Now it is right.”
talk: Nadalin makes the oars for the Doge’s barge and for half the smugglers in the lagoon, and will not say which pay sooner.
“A boat is a box,” Nadalin says. “The oar is the craft.”

people.name: Fantin Dobl
people.title: Money-Changer of the Calle
people.hint: a man ringing coins on a stone, one after another
people.meet: He rings one twice and sets it aside. “Fantin Dobl. That one is Thoolman, and clipped. Everybody clips.”
talk: Fantin can tell a mint by the ring and a forger by the hesitation.
“I do not make money,” Fantin says. “I only stand where it turns round.”

people.name: Samaritana Pevr
people.title: Garbler of Spice
people.hint: a woman sifting pepper with a cloth over her nose
people.meet: She pulls the cloth down. “Samaritana Pevr. I take the dust and the stones out. You would be surprised at the stones.”
talk: Samaritana says every sack is a tenth heavier leaving Thoolma than arriving here, and nobody is to blame.
“It is worth its weight,” Samaritana says. “So people add weight.”

people.name: Ortensia Burat
people.title: Puppet-Mistress of the Barge
people.hint: a woman with a puppet on each hand, arguing with both
people.meet: The left puppet bows. “Ortensia Burat,” says the right one. “She does the voices.”
talk: Ortensia’s puppets say what nobody in Marre may say with a face on.
“A puppet cannot be sent to the Leads,” Ortensia says. “I have asked.”

people.name: Marcuola Stali
people.title: Steward of the Barcaroli
people.hint: a broad woman chalking names on a slate and rubbing one out
people.meet: “He overcharged a senator,” she says, of the name. “Marcuola Stali. A senator! There are foreigners for that.”
talk: Marcuola knows who was rowed where last night, and has been offered money to say.
“A gondolier sees everything and has seen nothing,” Marcuola says.

people.name: Pierina Stopp
people.title: Hostess of the Bell
people.hint: a woman pouring a row of cups before the door has opened
people.meet: The bell rings. “Stand clear,” she says. Afterwards: “Pierina Stopp. A galley a day, and a barrel an hour.”
talk: Pierina says the Arsenal’s secrets are safe because its men only talk about each other.
“They build the fleet,” Pierina says. “I launch the builders.”

people.name: Simon Canev
people.title: Rope-Maker of the Walk
people.hint: a man walking backwards with hemp round his waist
people.meet: He does not turn. “Simon Canev. I have walked to Thoolma and back in this shed, and never seen where I was going.”
talk: Simon tests every cable by hanging from it, and says that is the only honest way.
“A ship is hung on my work,” Simon says.

people.name: Gnese Verz
people.title: Gardener of the Orti
people.hint: a woman cutting artichokes into a basket on her hip
people.meet: “Take one,” she says. “Gnese Verz. The city thinks food comes from the Rialto.”
talk: Gnese says salt wind makes the sweetest artichokes and the sourest gardeners.
“A hundred islands of stone,” Gnese says, “and one of dirt. Guess which they would miss.”

people.name: Madre Lucrezia Pist
people.title: Mother of the Foundlings
people.hint: a brisk woman with a baby on one arm and a ledger under the other
people.meet: “This one came at midnight,” she says. “Madre Lucrezia. We name them after the day. There are a great many Sundays.”
talk: Lucrezia says half the choirs and a third of the counting-houses of Marre learned their notes and numbers here.
“The Matron keeps what the city leaves,” Lucrezia says.

people.name: Mafio Parad
people.title: Ferryman of the Giglio
people.hint: a man who rows standing, facing forward, and talks the whole way
people.meet: “Stand in the middle,” he says. “Mafio Parad. Only foreigners sit.”
talk: Mafio has crossed the same hundred yards of water for thirty years and says it is never the same twice.
“The Families have water-gates,” Mafio says. “Everyone else has me.”

people.name: Giacomina Scov
people.title: Laundress of the Rio
people.hint: a woman wringing a sheet with a great house’s crest on it
people.meet: “Look,” she says, holding up a wine stain. “Somebody had a good night. Giacomina Scov. I know all of them by their linen.”
talk: Giacomina says a house’s troubles show in the wash a month before they show at the front door.
“Up there they wear masks,” Giacomina says. “Down here I wash what is under them.”

people.name: Agostin Mezan
people.title: Steward of the house
people.hint: a careful man straightening a picture that was already straight
people.meet: “Do not lean on that,” he says. “It is new. Everything is. Agostin Mezan. I serve the house.”
talk: Agostin has served an old house and a new one, and says the new one counts the spoons.
“Money takes a year,” Agostin says. “A name takes a hundred.”

people.name: Rocco Sabion
people.title: Bargeman of the Sand
people.hint: a man shovelling white sand in an easy, endless swing
people.meet: “Glass is sand, ash and a secret,” he says. “Rocco Sabion. I bring the sand. Nobody tells me the secret.”
talk: Rocco has landed sand here for twenty years and never been past the second shed.
“I can leave,” Rocco says. “That is the difference between us.”

people.name: Maddalena Perl
people.title: Bead-Stringer of the Row
people.hint: a woman dipping a fan of wires into a tray of beads
people.meet: She lifts the wires, full. “Maddalena Perl. Forty strings before noon. Talk if you like. I do not need my eyes for it.”
talk: Maddalena says the beads are worth more across the sea than the pepper that comes back.
“The masters make mirrors for doges,” Maddalena says. “We make money.”

people.name: Domenego Sofi
people.title: Master of the Isle, retired
people.hint: an old man with burn-scarred forearms, blowing a soap bubble through a straw
people.meet: The bubble floats off. “My lungs still know how,” he says. “Domenego Sofi. Forty years at the furnace. Now I do that.”
talk: Domenego can describe a mirror he made in his youth, and says it hangs in a palace he will never see.
“They buried the secret in us,” Domenego says. “So they must keep the graves close.”

people.name: Polo Segn
people.title: Signalman of Goat Rock
people.hint: a man hauling a flag up hand over hand, squinting east
people.meet: “Two sail, friendly, slow,” he says, and makes fast. “Polo Segn. I tell the castle what is coming. They decide if it is welcome.”
talk: Polo has not been off the rock since spring, and says the goats have better manners than the garrison.
“Both empires sail past me,” Polo says. “Neither waves.”

people.name: Olivo Tuff
people.title: Foreman of the Salvage
people.hint: a sunburnt man reading the tide off a notched pole
people.meet: “An hour,” he says. “Then it is over our heads again. Olivo Tuff. We work when the sea lets us.”
talk: Olivo says half the new palazzi stand on steps somebody else carved, long ago.
“We do not ask who built it,” Olivo says. “We ask what it weighs.”

people.name: Fosca Spong
people.title: Diver of the Raft
people.hint: a woman breathing slowly with her eyes shut, a stone in her lap
people.meet: She opens her eyes. “Do not talk to a diver before she goes down. Fosca Spong. After, I will talk all you like.”
talk: Fosca has walked on the drowned square and says the statues watch you leave.
“Forty feet is not far,” Fosca says. “Except straight down.”

people.name: Bernardo Oli
people.title: Oil-Carrier of the Cove
people.hint: a man with a jar on his back and a hand on the rope
people.meet: He sets the jar down with care. “Bernardo Oli. Forty jars a month. The lamp drinks more than I do.”
talk: Bernardo says he has kept more ships off the rocks than any captain, one jar at a time.
“If I stop, the lamp stops,” Bernardo says. “So I do not stop.”

people.name: Meneghina Sies
people.title: Gardener of the villa
people.hint: a woman on her knees with shears, clipping a hedge to a string
people.meet: “They come for six weeks,” she says. “I am here for fifty-two. Meneghina Sies. The garden is for them. The work is for me.”
talk: Meneghina says the family walks the paths once, admires them, and goes in to play cards.
“A hedge is a wall that needs feeding,” Meneghina says.

people.name: Nardo Val
people.title: Fowler of the Marsh
people.hint: a man lying flat in a punt, moving only his eyes
people.meet: A long silence, then a whisper. “Nardo Val. Lie down or go away. They can see a man standing from the city.”
talk: Nardo sells duck to the villas and sleeps under the punt, turned over.
“The mosquitoes are the rent,” Nardo says.

people.name: Togna Pil
people.title: Rice-Wife of the Floors
people.hint: a woman turning grain with a wooden rake and watching the sky
people.meet: “If it rains, we run,” she says. “Togna Pil. A wet floor is a lost month.”
talk: Togna can smell rain an hour off and has never lost a floor.
“The city eats it with saffron,” Togna says. “We eat it with more rice.”

people.name: Zanina Febr
people.title: Keeper of the Chapel
people.hint: a thin woman ladling something bitter into a row of cups
people.meet: “Drink,” she says. “It is vile. Zanina Febr. The Lazaretto sends the bark. I send the prayers. Between us some of them live.”
talk: Zanina has had the fever six times and says it gets bored.
“The Matron loves the city,” Zanina says. “I remind her the city eats.”

people.name: Tranquillo Ost
people.title: Host of the Locanda
people.hint: a slow, smiling man carrying a pot too heavy to hurry with
people.meet: “Sit,” he says. “It will be ready when it is ready. Tranquillo Ost. My mother named me well.”
talk: Tranquillo hears every buyer’s best price by the second jug, and has never used it.
“Silk makes men whisper,” Tranquillo says. “Wine fixes that.”

people.name: Vido Fornas
people.title: Brick-Burner of the Kilns
people.hint: a man reading the colour of a fire through a spy-hole
people.meet: “Cherry,” he says, and shuts the hole. “Vido Fornas. Too pale is mud. Too dark is glass. Cherry is brick.”
talk: Vido says the Isles get the glory and the kilns get the palaces to hold up.
“Nobody looks at a brick,” Vido says. “They look at what it keeps out of the water.”

people.name: Zamaria Zatt
people.title: Raftsman of the River
people.hint: a man walking across floating logs as if across a floor
people.meet: He steps from log to log without looking. “Zamaria Zatt. Do not try it. The river keeps the ones who try.”
talk: Zamaria lives on his raft for a month coming down and sells his house at the end of every journey.
“The city stands on a forest,” Zamaria says. “Upside down.”

people.name: Battista Maz
people.title: Leader of the pile-gang
people.hint: a hoarse man singing a line and letting eight others answer with a blow
people.meet: He finishes the verse. “Battista Maz. I do not lift. I sing. It is harder than it looks.”
talk: Battista knows two hundred verses and says a pile wants about ninety.
“My grandfather sang this island up,” Battista says, pointing at the city.

people.name: Orsolina Sal
people.title: Salt-Raker of the Pans
people.hint: a barefoot woman pushing a wide board through shallow brine
people.meet: “Hat,” she says, pointing at the sun. “Orsolina Sal. It will cook you as it cooks the sea.”
talk: Orsolina says the Republic taxes salt harder than gold, because everyone needs it.
“The sea gives it away,” Orsolina says. “The Republic sells it.”

people.name: Cristofolo Peoc
people.title: Mussel-Man of the Poles
people.hint: a man twisting a rope of mussels off a pole with both arms
people.meet: “Mind your hands,” he says. “They cut. Cristofolo Peoc. Three years to grow a pole, an hour to strip it.”
talk: Cristofolo says he farms the sea, and the fishermen say he only waits.
“A fisherman chases,” Cristofolo says. “I plant.”

people.name: Ferigo Fang
people.title: Master of the Dredger
people.hint: a mud-spattered man sounding the channel with a marked pole
people.meet: “A hand shallower than last month,” he says. “Ferigo Fang. The lagoon is always trying to become a field.”
talk: Ferigo says if he stopped for ten years the galleys would be rowing through grass.
“Doges come and go,” Ferigo says. “Mud stays. So do I.”

people.name: Anzoleta Lum
people.title: Lamp-Keeper of the Shrine
people.hint: a young woman in a skiff, filling small lamps from a can
people.meet: “One going, one coming,” she says. “Anzoleta Lum. I count them at dusk. The numbers should match.”
talk: Anzoleta says in a bad year there are lamps left over, and she lights those too.
“The Matron cannot see in the dark either,” Anzoleta says.

people.name: Jacopo Tartan
people.title: Fisherman of the Bar
people.hint: a man painting his door a red that hurts to look at
people.meet: “So I know it,” he says. “Jacopo Tartan. My neighbour is yellow. We do not speak.”
talk: Jacopo fishes the open sea and says lagoon fish taste of the city.
“We are the wall,” Jacopo says. “The sea has to get past us first.”

people.name: Zaccaria Bomb
people.title: Sergeant of the Sea-Gate
people.hint: a stout man greasing a chain link with great tenderness
people.meet: “She has not gone up since my grandfather,” he says. “Zaccaria Bomb. She will go up tomorrow if the Doge says.”
talk: Zaccaria drills the garrison every week against a fleet that has never come.
“A chain you never use is the best kind,” Zaccaria says.

people.name: Lorenza Fum
people.title: Fumigator of the Sheds
people.hint: a woman in a waxed coat, turning bales with a long hook
people.meet: “Do not touch,” she says, through a cloth. “Day twelve. Lorenza Fum. On day forty you may hug it.”
talk: Lorenza has handled a fortune in silk and never once with her hands.
“The merchants hate me for forty days,” Lorenza says. “Then they forget me for a year.”

people.name: Hieronimo Fed
people.title: Writer to the Proveditors
people.hint: a clerk holding a letter with tongs over a dish of vinegar
people.meet: He reads it at arm’s length. “Hieronimo Fed. Port of sailing? Deaths aboard? Do not hand me anything.”
talk: Hieronimo has been offered gold for a clean bill and says the vinegar is for that, too.
“One false stamp,” Hieronimo says, “and the Republic is a graveyard with good views.”

people.name: Fra Serafin
people.title: Brother of the Deaf Bell
people.hint: a small monk hauling on a bell-rope and wincing at the result
people.meet: Clank. “It was cast wrong,” he says. “Fra Serafin. We could not afford another, and now we are fond of it.”
talk: Serafin says boatmen steer by the clank in fog, because no other bell sounds so bad.
“The Matron hears intention,” Serafin says. “Luckily.”

people.name: Pasquetta Zuc
people.title: Stallwoman of the Raft
people.hint: a woman selling pumpkins from a boat so full she is sitting on them
people.meet: “Careful, the plank moves,” she says. “Pasquetta Zuc. Everything here was in the ground yesterday.”
talk: Pasquetta rows two hours each way and says the city pays double for the dew.
“By the time the senators wake,” Pasquetta says, “we have fed them and gone.”

people.name: Sandro Sepa
people.title: Cuttle-Catcher of the Flats
people.hint: an old man with a lantern and a small three-pronged spear
people.meet: “Follow the sticks,” he says. “Sandro Sepa. I have walked here sixty years. The mud took my brother in the first.”
talk: Sandro sells the ink to the scriveners and the rest to the cooks.
“The tide gives you two hours,” Sandro says. “It does not give three.”

people.name: Liberal Bronz
people.title: Founder of the Isle
people.hint: a man with his ear against a new bell, tapping it with a knuckle
people.meet: He listens, and nods. “She will do. Liberal Bronz. You get one pour. If it is wrong you break it and weep.”
talk: Liberal cast the anchor of the Doge’s barge and a bell for a house of monks who could not pay.
“Metal remembers how it was poured,” Liberal says.

people.name: Momola Scorz
people.title: Tanner of the Isle
people.hint: a woman scraping a hide over a beam with a two-handled knife
people.meet: “You will stop noticing,” she says. “Momola Scorz. Then you go to the city and they notice for you.”
talk: Momola says the Ten Families all wear her gloves and none would cross to thank her.
“A year in the pit,” Momola says. “Leather cannot be hurried. Neither can I.”

people.name: Cecilia Merl
people.title: Lace-Maker of the Isle
people.hint: a woman moving a dozen bobbins without seeming to choose among them
people.meet: “A thumb’s width a day,” she says. “Cecilia Merl. A collar is a season. A bride’s veil is a winter and my eyes.”
talk: Cecilia says the pattern came from mending nets, and the nets are still better made.
“He knots to catch fish,” Cecilia says. “I knot to catch senators’ wives.”

people.name: Ambrogio Ostreg
people.title: Oysterman of the Beds
people.hint: a man opening an oyster with a twist and holding it out
people.meet: “Eat,” he says. “Ambrogio Ostreg. Now you know why I sleep with a crossbow.”
talk: Ambrogio counts his beds every dawn and has names for the thieves he has not caught.
“Three years growing,” Ambrogio says. “Gone in a swallow.”

people.name: Rigo Coral
people.title: Coral-Diver of the Rock
people.hint: a man with a net bag at his belt and ears that do not quite work
people.meet: He speaks too loudly. “Rigo Coral! The deep took my hearing. It was a fair price.”
talk: Rigo says the best coral is always one breath deeper than is wise.
“Red for the saints,” Rigo says. “And for the men who fetch it.”

people.name: Lunardo Zorz
people.title: Keeper of the Files
people.hint: a stooped man carrying a file box as if it were a child
people.meet: “Do not touch,” he says, mildly. “Ask. Lunardo Zorz. Everything in this room is in order, and I am the order.”
talk: Lunardo can find any name in the lagoon in the time it takes to say it.
“A file is a person who cannot argue,” Lunardo says. “Be fair to it.”

people.name: Chiara Dand
people.title: Constable of the Cerdans
people.hint: a square-shouldered woman who stands where she can see both doors
people.meet: “You walk too fast,” she says. “People look at fast.” A nod. “Chiara Dand. Constable. Slow down and you will see more.”
talk: Chiara has walked the Piazza every day for nine years and can tell a stranger by his shoes.
“Arrest the right one,” Chiara says. “The Capo forgives slow. He does not forgive wrong.”

people.name: Felicita Brol
people.title: Mirror-Scryer of the Cerdans
people.hint: a pale young woman who blinks in daylight like someone come up from a cellar
people.meet: “You are standing in my light,” she says, though the room has none. “Felicita Brol. I watch the glasses. Do not ask what I see.”
talk: Felicita says the mirrors show what is there, which on feast nights is less than you would think.
“The Blind Mirror sees further than any of us,” Felicita says. “I only see sooner.”

activities.name: Assign the staff
activities.text: Who lays the fires, who carries water, and who is kept away from the legate.

activities.name: Attend the family
activities.text: Be where you are wanted a moment before you are wanted there.

activities.name: Accounts and the cellar
activities.text: Candles, oats, wine and wages, each in its column, and the columns made to agree.

activities.name: Dinner service
activities.text: The high table first, the salt in its place, and no dish set down with a sound.

activities.name: Tally bales
activities.text: Count them in, in whichever language the ledger wants.

activities.name: Dice in the back room
activities.text: Three bones, a cup, and a table that remembers debts.

activities.name: Tie the vines
